content:
maya: PR #8342 ready for merge — performance canary shows p95 tail increase on long-seq. Need quick eyes & decision on alloc window. Bench logs: https://rddw.co/gist/8342-bench

bench-bot: Automated perf run complete (run id: perf-2024-11-04-09). Summary:
```
baseline: master
  long-seq p50=120ms p95=210ms p99=480ms
  throughput=145 tok/s
  mem p95=7.8GB
PR 8342 (this branch):
  long-seq p50=125ms p95=320ms p99=610ms (+52% p95)
  throughput=138 tok/s (-4.8%)
  mem p95=8.6GB (+10%)
notes: tail skew on microbatch path, increased KV cache misses by ~18%
```

ian: Do we have the microbatch config diff? suspect batch horizon change. Link to diff: https://rddw.co/patch/8342

frank: Looking at the diff — changed scheduler heuristic + lowered batch horizon. Could explain tail.

maya: I can try a quick microbench with `MICROBATCH_SIZE=16` vs 32 and post numbers.

olivia: Reminder: release window closes 3pm PST. If we don't merge before then we delay next week's canary.

frank: I can run microbench now on canary pool. ping me once it's pushed.

bench-bot: microbench queued (id: micro-8342-1). ETA ~12m.

bench-bot: microbench results:
```
MICROBATCH=32 -> p95=320ms
MICROBATCH=16 -> p95=210ms (aligned with baseline)
throughput @16: 122 tok/s (vs 145 baseline)
mem p95 @16: 7.9GB
```

frank: Looks like reducing microbatch recovers tail but costs throughput. Tradeoff: latency vs cost.

ian: Could we do a targeted change: revert batch horizon only, keep scheduler heuristics? That might keep throughput.

maya: I'll prepare a follow-up patch that reverts batch-horizon tweak and pins microbatch to 16 for canary. Need 2 approvals to merge 8342 -> canary.

olivia: I can approve for canary if we set alloc window to 2h and add an auto-revert job on perf regression >10% p95.

ian: Approved for canary with alloc=2h and auto-revert rule. :+1:

frank: Approved for canary too. I'll run the canary once merged.

maya: thanks all — merging after approvals, will follow up with canary link and heatmap when ready. :pray:
